definitions.explanation: A casual conjunction used to contrast or introduce an exception. Used at the beginning of sentences.
When attached to nouns, means 'even' (e.g., {子供|こども}でも - even a child).

examples.japanese: {行|い}きたい。でも、{時間|じかん}がない。
examples.english: I want to go. But I don't have time.

examples.japanese: でも、それは{本当|ほんとう}ですか。
{高|たか}いです。でも、おいしいです。
{疲|つか}れました。でも、{楽|たの}しかったです。
examples.english: I'm tired. But it was fun.

examples.japanese: あの{店|みせ}は{少|すこ}し{遠|とお}いです。でも、{料理|りょうり}がとてもおいしいので、{週末|しゅうまつ}によく{行|い}きます。
examples.english: That shop is a bit far. But the food is very delicious, so I often go there on weekends.

examples.japanese: お{茶|ちゃ}でも{飲|の}みませんか。
examples.english: Would you like to have some tea or something?

examples.japanese: このゲームは{簡単|かんたん}なので、{初|はじ}めてでもすぐに{上手|じょうず}になれますよ。
examples.english: This game is simple, so even if it's your first time, you'll get good at it quickly.

notes: でも is a casual conjunction used at the start of sentences to introduce contrast. It's softer than しかし (however) and more conversational. When attached to nouns (〜でも), it means 'even' or 'or something like.' {何|なに}でもいい means 'anything is fine.'
